narrative:
**Engagement fell sharply across the board.** Model downloads came in at 2.28M for the week (22,069 models tracked), down 39.5% from roughly 3.77M the prior week, and model likes dropped 60.7% to 5,901 from about 15,000. Space likes were softer but more stable, at 541 across 5,958 spaces (-17.9% from roughly 659). The pullback was mirrored on the supply side: Qwen-family models fell 21.2% to 6,261 and "other-open" fell 18.0% to 5,110, while Llama was the only large family to grow, up 3.9% to 1,071. Smaller families moved on thin bases — GLM/Zhipu halved to 139 (-52.6%), DeepSeek rose to 98 (+21.0%), Nemotron to 86 (+16.2%), and Kimi/Moonshot slipped to 21 (-27.6%). One methodology caveat dominates the family cut: 8,529 of 22,069 models (38.6%) remain unclassified as "unknown," so family-level shares should be read as directional only.

**Spaces activity rotated toward analytical and educational use cases.** Education spaces rose 22.4% to 240, document-AI 15.7% to 419, and data-analysis 14.8% to 495, while image-generation fell 7.9% to 556, music-generation fell 20% to 52 (from 65), and the large "other" bucket fell 7.5% to 1,874. Chat-assistant held roughly flat at 895 (-2.1%) and remained the largest labeled category at 15.0% share. Vertical penetration echoed this: education reached 8.19% of spaces (+18.7%), cybersecurity 2.23% (+24.6%), and healthcare 4.70% (+15.6%), against consumer at 8.66% (-16.5%) and enterprise-productivity at 6.24% (-6.6%). On technology tags, tool-use (3.61%, +18.2%), local-inference (2.17%, +18.7%), and fine-tuned (3.19%, +15.1%) gained, while diffusion (4.40%, -11.6%), RAG (2.23%, -12.1%), and agentic (6.33%, -5.4%) receded; the eye-catching long-context jump (+68.6%) sits on just 0.34% of spaces, or about 20 items, and MoE (0.79%, +32.1%) is similarly thin.

**Within chat assistants (n=551), Qwen's share slipped to 23.8% from about 32% while "other-open" rose to 43.6% and Llama to 8.2%; proprietary APIs eased to 12.3%.** Qwen still led coding (36.7% of 128 coding spaces, down modestly), and several per-use-case family movements — 3D/gaming (n=31), music-generation (n=23), education (n=34), and robotics (n=14) — rest on denominators small enough that single-space changes swing the percentages, so treat those deltas as noise rather than signal. SDK mix was mostly stable: static 3,257 (+2.8%), Gradio 2,063 (-5.5%), Docker 482 (-11.6%), Streamlit 93 (+25.7% on a small base). Next week, watch whether the downloads and likes decline reverses — a two-week confirmation would separate a genuine slowdown from a one-week collection or holiday-period artifact — and whether the education/document-AI build-out in Spaces holds.
